title: Take an ear temperature: seat the covered probe snugly in a manikin's ear canal and hold it still through the reading
instruction: Take the manikin's left-ear temperature: seat the probe snugly in the canal, press Measure, keep it still until the beep, then lay the thermometer down.
context: Nursing assistants (O*NET 31-1131.00: 'Record vital signs, such as temperature...'; 1.51M US jobs), medical assistants (31-9092.00: 'measure their vital signs'; 0.83M) and LPNs (29-2061.00: 'Measure and record patients' vital signs, such as... temperature'; 0.67M) take a temperature at every vital-signs round, on hospital units mostly with a tympanic thermometer. Its directions: place the probe snugly in the ear canal aimed at the opposite temple, keep it steady, press and release MEASURE; a long beep ends the 2-3 s reading, and if the probe moves it shows POS and gives no reading. A probe not sealed or not aimed reads low. One hand holds the 146 g device at arm's length with a 6 mm cone in a 9 x 7.5 mm canal on a slanted axis, while the other hand's press on MEASURE pushes on it. Unlike clipping a spring oximeter onto a finger, nothing clamps here: alignment and stillness through a timed reading are held by the hand alone.
setup: Metres; world x forward, y left, z up; origin midway between the arm bases (0, +/-0.305, 0.750); station table top z = 0.7475; heights below are above the table top. (1) Ear-examination manikin, fixed (two G-clamps on its base): Kyoto Kagaku MW12 EAR Examination Simulator II: a life-size adult head (soft light skin-tone resin, moulded closed-eyed face) on a charcoal shoulder bust, 420 x 220 x 382 mm (catalogue 42 x 22 x 39 cm), 1.75 kg, normal exam ears (L1/R1) fitted, neck upright, power on in self-learning mode. Base centred at (0.2685, -0.010), facing +y (looking to the robot's left), so its left ear faces the robot. Head 152 mm wide, 192 mm front to back, 230 mm tall, centre (0.2685, 0.006, 0.267); shoulders 420 mm wide, 105 mm high at the shoulder points. Left ear canal: entrance an ellipse 9 mm tall x 7.5 mm front to back, centred at (0.195, 0.000, 0.255), at the bottom of a concha bowl 21 mm across and 2.5 mm deep; the canal is 25 mm deep and runs into the head along (0.951, 0.255, 0.174): inward, 15 deg toward the face and 10 deg up, toward the right temple. The auricle (62 x 34 mm) sits behind and around the opening, its rim 1-4 mm proud of the skull (see fidelity). (2) Tympanic ear thermometer, free: Braun ThermoScan PRO 6000 (Welch Allyn/Hillrom 06000-200), white ABS, 152 x 44 x 33 mm, 146 g (100 g plus two AA cells). Body a rounded 44 x 33 mm bar 127 mm long, then a 10 mm dome to a 22 x 20 mm top; the probe stands 16.5 mm proud of the top, bent 20 deg toward the back: a 16 mm blue collar, then the covered cone, 12 mm across at its base and 6 mm at its tip. A new ThermoScan PRO 6000 probe cover (06000-005, clear polypropylene) is already on; the thermometer is awake and ready (three dashes, green ring). MEASURE: an 18 mm round button centred 118 mm from the base end on the display face, 1.5 mm proud, 1 mm travel, 1.5 N to start and 1.8 N at the bottom. Display window 28 x 26 mm centred 93 mm from the base; C/F and Mem keys at 70 mm; timer button at 47 mm. It lies on its back (display up) on the table, body along +x, probe toward +x, base end at (0.090, -0.200), axis 16.5 mm above the table. Friction (static/dynamic): thermometer 0.6/0.5, manikin skin 0.6/0.5. Nothing else is on the table. Both arms start at the ready pose with the grippers open. Full dimension tables and sources in the README.
scoring: Read every 50 ms step from the thermometer's pose, its MEASURE button travel and the grippers' joint states. SEATED: the cover tip at least 2 mm past the canal entrance plane (a snug cover reaches 3.5 mm), within 3 mm of the canal axis, the probe axis within 20 deg of the canal axis. HELD: a gripper's centre point inside the thermometer's bounding box, pads at least 10% closed. MEASURING (the directions for use): pressing MEASURE (travel 0.7 mm or more) while seated and held starts it; from the button's release (travel under 0.3 mm for 0.1 s) the probe must stay seated and held, its tip moving less than 1.5 mm and its axis turning less than 3 deg from their pose at release, for 3.0 s (the PRO 6000 measures for 2-3 s); then the reading is taken (long beep, temperature shown). If it unseats, is let go or moves more during the measurement, it shows POS and no reading is possible for the rest of the run (it needs a new cover). Pressing MEASURE while not seated measures room air and uses up the cover: no reading for the rest of the run. LAID DOWN: after the reading, the thermometer rests on the table (lowest point within 5 mm of the table top, cover tip at least 20 mm out of the canal), released (each gripper centre at least 30 mm from its bounding box) and still (under 0.01 m/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 1 s. Score at the end of the run: 1.0 reading taken and the thermometer laid down; 0.75 reading taken, thermometer not laid down (held, in the ear, moving); 0.5 a measurement was started on a seated probe but gave no reading (POS or unfinished); 0.25 the probe was seated for 1 s or more at some time but no measurement was started on it (a room-air press included); otherwise 0. Sticky 0 for the rest of the run: the cover tip ever more than 12 mm inside the canal (the MW12's painful-insertion zone), or any part of the thermometer ever more than 20 mm below the table top (dropped off the table). Success = 1.0, held a further 1 s. Real trial: the thermometer's display decides the reading (a temperature or LO counts, as the manikin is at room temperature; POS or an error doesn't); the MW12 in self-learning mode beeps when an instrument tip passes the bony canal (the sticky depth zero); seating, the press (single beep) and the hold to the long beep are judged from video; a photo shows the thermometer released on the table.
run_limit: 1,800 steps (90 s at 20 Hz); the scripted demo reaches success at about step 570 (28.5 s)
reset_notes: Eject the used cover over a bin and push a new cover onto the probe from the box kept off the table; wait for the ready signal (three dashes, green ring); lay the thermometer back on its back on its tape marks (base end at the mark, probe toward the manikin's side of the table). The manikin stays clamped. In simulation, reset restores all poses and clears the measuring state.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The manikin is rigid: its soft ear is a rigid shell with a rigid elliptical canal, and its auricle is modelled low (1-4 mm proud) so the thermometer head clears it, where the real soft auricle folds under the head. The cover is part of the probe (no ejection). MEASURE is a sprung slider. The reading is task code following the directions for use (press while seated, then 3 s steady, else POS); no infrared or temperature is simulated.
